title: A `tRNS` sample the image's bit depth cannot contain
why: `tRNS` stores its samples as 16-bit values whatever the bit depth, and at depth 8 the range is 0–255 — so `0x01ff` names a sample no pixel can hold. Not a harmless spare byte: reading the low half alone makes a real pixel transparent, while a decoder honouring the range finds no match and leaves it opaque. Two rasters from one hash-valid file, and the difference lands straight in the candidate gate.
